correctness.rationale: For the stated discrete copying rule, each discordant edge {u,v} contributes w_uv(b_u+b_v)/(2nD) to conditional drift of M=Σd_uX_u/D, irrespective of orientation. Vanishing from every configuration is equivalent to every cut sum zero; singleton cuts at u,v and pair {u,v} isolate 2w_uv(b_u+b_v), forcing b_u+b_v=0 per edge. Connectedness gives alternating ±h on bipartite graphs, or h=0 with an odd cycle. All nonzero copying rates yield finite-state a.s. consensus, and a bounded stopped martingale gives P(all+)=M_0. Polarized bipartite initial condition has M=1/2 because each side accounts for half total weighted degrees; first flip is geometric with probability (1-h)/2 and expected time 2/(1-h), equality on K2.
